short_summary: Following a fatal shooting attack that claimed the lives of two soldiers near Hebron, Israeli security forces initiated a multi-day counterterrorism operation across the city.

sources.name: Maariv
sources.title: בעקבות הפיגוע הקטלני: צה"ל פתח במבצע בחברון - "עתיד להימשך מספר ימים"

paragraphs: Following a lethal shooting attack near Hebron that claimed the lives of two Israeli soldiers, the Israel Defense Forces and the Shin Bet security agency initiated a targeted, multi-day counterterrorism operation across the city. The assault occurred at Yehuda Junction along Route 35, where two armed assailants exited their vehicle and confronted security personnel stationed at a checkpoint, sparking an intense gun battle that lasted more than twenty minutes. The fallen soldiers were identified as Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roitman, 23, from Ashkelon, and Sergeant Yuval Shai Swilim, 20, from Hod Hasharon. Three additional soldiers sustained minor injuries during the prolonged engagement before reinforcements, including a deputy battalion commander and a company commander, outflanked and neutralized both gunmen.

Roitman and Swilim served in the Ari Battalion, designated as the 775th Battalion within the Home Front Command’s Search and Rescue Brigade. Formed over the past year to augment combat personnel, the unit had commenced its inaugural operational deployment only days before the confrontation. Roitman and Swilim represent the battalion’s first fatalities since its inception. Security officials subsequently identified the slain assailants as Hamouda al-Jaaba and Firas al-Jaaba, two 27-year-old relatives residing near one another within the same local clan in Hebron.

Preliminary investigations indicated that the attackers arrived equipped with an M16 assault rifle, a handgun, and considerable stores of ammunition and magazines. Security assessments suggested that the gunmen had initially intended to assault civilian motorists or infiltrate nearby settlements along Route 35. However, upon recognizing the robust military posture along the primary traffic arteries, they altered their trajectory and fired upon the roadside checkpoint instead. A senior military officer emphasized that while the standoff extracted a heavy toll, the garrison’s stance averted a catastrophic assault against civilian targets. Authorities are examining whether the gunmen acted independently or operated under external guidance.

In response, the Judea Brigade mobilized alongside the Shin Bet, Border Police, and Judea District Coordination and Liaison office to conduct exhaustive searches targeting dozens of locations tied to the clan. Movement in the operational sector was heavily restricted, with residents permitted to exit exclusively through three dedicated checkpoints subject to meticulous screening. Concurrently, security forces enforced closures across Hebron and nearby Halhul, enacted vehicle inspections under the "Grey Bolt" protocol, and systematically dismantled illegal structures deemed security hazards near the encounter site. Counterterrorism measures were simultaneously heightened across Jenin, Nablus, and Jericho.

Visiting the scene alongside Defense Minister Israel Katz, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to expand operations within the perpetrators' neighborhoods, citing operational models previously applied in regional refugee camps, involving comprehensive door-to-door inspections and the dismantling of militant infrastructure. IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir noted that military forces had preemptively prepared for escalation across Judea and Samaria, reinforcing the sector and activating the 98th Division headquarters to contain broader threats.

facts.fact: Two IDF soldiers, Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roitman and Sergeant Yuval Shai Swilim, were killed and three others lightly wounded in a shooting attack at Yehuda Junction on Route 35 near Hebron.
The two attackers, identified as Hamouda al-Jaaba and Firas al-Jaaba, both 27 from Hebron, were killed after an exchange of fire lasting more than 20 minutes.

The fallen soldiers served in the Ari Battalion (775) of the Home Front Command's Search and Rescue Brigade, which was established within the past year and had just begun its first operational deployment.
Following the attack, the IDF, Shin Bet, Border Police, and Judea DCO launched a targeted counterterrorism operation in Hebron expected to last several days.
Local residents in the operational area were restricted to exiting via three designated checkpoints subject to security screening.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz visited the attack site, where Netanyahu announced plans to apply the refugee camp operational model in the perpetrators' neighborhoods.
Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir stated that the military had prepared for potential escalation across Judea and Samaria, reinforcing forces and activating the 98th Division headquarters.
